coreutils — cat

Part of a campaign reimplementing common utilities with parity harnesses. Worth reading for the ordinary shape of a CLI package: argument annotations, file I/O through Norma, and error handling on the ⇥ channel.

Source: examples/coreutils/packages/cat

src/main.fab#

One file of a multi-file package: it refers to siblings that are not shown here.

# =============================================================================
# cat — concatenate files and print to stdout
# =============================================================================
#
# What this example teaches:
#   • Recursive fn — cat_stdin calls itself to process lines until EOF
#   • string ∪ none — nullable read return for end-of-stream detection
#   • for from solum.carpe — file line iteration via the only stdlib
#   • if branch — dispatching stdin vs file mode based on operand count
#   • describe/proba — testing mode selection without I/O
#
# Syntaxes used:
#   • import — lines 1-2
#   • fn … → bool — line 4
#   • fn … → void — lines 10, 18, 23
#   • return — lines 4, 30, 32
#   • if / else — lines 14, 21, 28-29
#   • for from — lines 20, 24
#   • read (built-in) — line 14
#   • var / const — throughout
#   • ≡ / is not — lines 5, 13, 14
#   • vel (default) — line 16
#   • describe / test / assert — lines 30-33
#   • ∪ none — line 13
#   • @ cli / @ description / @ operand — lines 38-40
#   • main — line 41
#
# Alternate approaches (not shown):
#   • recursive stdin read vs do/dum true iterative loop — avoids stack growth for large input (alternates doc §Recursive stdin read)
#
# Anti-patterns (avoid these):
#   • if condition must be bool — Faber requires explicit boolean conditions, no truthy/falsy coercion
#   • read returns string ∪ none — always check est none before use, vel for default fallback
#
# Learning path:
#   Before: pwd, yes
#   After:  head, tail, wc
#
# Stage: Stage 2-4, stdin/file parity
# Backend: stepper+Rust
# =============================================================================

import from "norma:fs" only
import from "§gnu/stdio" gnu_stdio

fn modus_stdin(list<string> operands) → bool {
    return operands.longitudo() ≡ 0
}

# read returns none at EOF, so recursion stops without printing a final
# synthetic line.
fn cat_stdin() → void {
    const string ∪ none linea ← read
    if linea is not none {
        gnu_stdio.scribe_linea(linea coalesce "")
        cat_stdin()
    }
}

fn cat_file(string path) → void {
    for from solum.carpe(path) const linea {
        gnu_stdio.scribe_linea(linea)
    }
}

fn cat_files(list<string> operands) → void {
    for from operands const path {
        cat_file(path)
    }
}

describe "cat operand mode" tag "coreutils" {
    test "no operands selects stdin mode" {
        assert modus_stdin([]) ≡ true
    }
    test "file operands select file mode" {
        assert modus_stdin(["input.txt"]) ≡ false
    }
}

@ cli "cat"
@ description "GNU coreutils cat stdin parity exemplum"
@ operand rest string operands
main args args {
    const list<string> operands ← args.operands
    const int count ← operands.longitudo()
    if count ≡ 0 {
        cat_stdin()
    }
    if count > 0 {
        cat_files(operands)
    }
}
